issues.description: The problem specification (UML and textual description) defines acceptSupplyDelivery with four parameters (supplier name, ingredient name, price, quantity): acceptSupplyDelivery(String, String, int, int). The provided solution implements acceptSupplyDelivery with only three parameters (ingredient name, price, quantity): acceptSupplyDelivery(String, int, int). This mismatch between the specification and the solution will confuse students about the required method signature and parameter order.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the specification and implementation. Either (A) update the problem statement/UML to define acceptSupplyDelivery as acceptSupplyDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity) (removing the supplier parameter), or (B) change the SealSaloon implementation to accept the supplier parameter as specified (e.g., acceptSupplyDelivery(String supplier, String name, int price, int quantity)) and ignore or store the supplier as needed. Ensure the method signature shown in the UML, the textual description, and the code are identical.

issues.description: The problem statement (diagram and text) specifies acceptSupplyDelivery should take four parameters (supplier name, ingredient name, price, quantity) and describes the supplier name as the first parameter. The provided solution implements acceptSupplyDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity) — a three-parameter signature where the single String parameter appears to be the ingredient name (named 'name') and the supplier parameter is missing. This mismatch between the expected four-parameter signature and the actual three-parameter implementation can confuse students about the required method signature and parameter meanings.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the implementation with the problem statement by changing the method signature to acceptSupplyDelivery(String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) and update the implementation to use ingredientName when adding/updating stock. Alternatively, update the problem statement to clearly state the intended three-parameter signature (ingredientName, price, quantity) if the supplier name is intentionally unused.
